en: Preface to the *Ke jin'gang bei* (The Diamond Scalpel of Sectioning), composed by the Śramaṇa Jingyue of Yunjian during the Song Dynasty.

The practice of dividing the chapters and sections of this Great Sūtra began with Pingshan Yao of Guannei; it was unheard of in previous generations. Our Patriarch Zhang’an further detailed these divisions in his commentary (*shu*). When it came to Jingxi, he divided the "Kāśyapa Chapter" into the [three] aspects of the True, the Conditioned, and the Perfect, specifically pointing out their respective domains. Thus...

The provisional and the real, the advanced and the rejected, are now clearly illuminated; one may truly say that the profound currents have been well distinguished and the layered meanings skillfully analyzed. I, moreover, have divided the current text based on the fact that Buddha-nature pervades the three thousand worlds and fully encompasses all things.

By further subdividing it—through the dialogue between guest and host and the citation of texts to explain their meaning—I have avoided even the slightest confusion. Though my legs are short, I am capable of encouraging the young disciples in the stream of the Dharma; I venture to take up this burden. Some may say: "Is this not like a cowherd’s woman adding water? Will it not dilute the flavor of the milk? Not so. Milk increases milk.
If one can churn it thoroughly, the *amṛta* (clarified butter) can be obtained; how could it remain merely milk?
